name: Executive Order of October 20, 1875 adding land north of the Yellowstone to the Crow reservation (Royce area 585)
citation: Executive Order of October 20, 1875 (Royce p. 882), revoked by Executive Order of March 8, 1876
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. On October 20, 1875 the President set apart an addition to the Crow reservation established by the treaty of May 7, 1868: land north of the Yellowstone from where 107 degrees west longitude crosses it, up to the mouth of Big Timber Creek, with no point of the strip less than 20 miles from the river (Royce p. 882).
On March 8, 1876 the President revoked the October 20, 1875 order and restored the tract to the public domain (Royce p. 884; Royce p. 883 remark: revoked and canceled).
today: The addition lasted under five months. The Indian Claims Commission's Crow land claim (Docket 54) concerns the 1868 cession; its findings read for this file do not mention this addition.

openQuestions: Revocation of an executive-order addition is not a breach by itself (Jordan, 2026-11-08); no finding about this tract was found.
Duplicate pair: the revoking order is cession-1876-03-08-crow, same Royce area 585.
Why the addition was made and revoked was not researched; the Crow Tribe's own account was not found.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 13): confirmed against the Royce p. 882 and p. 884 page scans (Oct. 20, 1875 bounds: Yellowstone at 107 W. up to Big Timber creek, no point less than 20 miles from the river; Mar. 8, 1876 revocation; p. 885 "See 585"). ICC full-text search "Crow Yellowstone 1875" found nothing on this addition; the Court of Claims Crow cases (81 Ct. Cl. 238, 1935; 151 Ct. Cl. 281, 1960) were listed and are not about it.
